sections.heading: What Is Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin?
body: Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin is a combination of two separate research peptides sold together as one Veracue offering. It is not a single molecule, and the two components are not chemically related. Tesamorelin is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), built on the same 44-amino-acid backbone as endogenous human GHRH, with an added stabilizing modification at the N-terminus. Ipamorelin is a synthetic pentapeptide -- five amino acids -- studied as a growth hormone secretagogue that acts through the ghrelin receptor (GHSR).

Because the two peptides work through different receptor systems, evidence collected on one does not automatically describe the other, and evidence on either peptide alone does not establish anything about how they behave when supplied together. This page treats those as three separate evidence questions: what is known about tesamorelin, what is known about ipamorelin, and what is known about the combination specifically. The last of those has the least available evidence, and this page says so plainly rather than blending the other two into an implied answer.

A note on naming: this material is referred to in some vendor and forum contexts as a 'tesa ipa blend' or 'stack.' Veracue uses the descriptive name Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin because 'blend' and 'stack' do not communicate a verified ratio or formulation, and because this page does not treat the combination as a validated protocol -- see Terminology, below.

sections.heading: Tesamorelin: Scientific Identity
body: Tesamorelin (research synonym TH9507 / TH-9507) is a synthetic 44-amino-acid peptide built on the sequence of human growth hormone-releasing hormone (hGHRH 1-44), carrying an N-terminal modification (a trans-3-hexenoyl group on the tyrosine residue) that increases resistance to enzymatic breakdown compared with native GHRH. It is studied as a GHRH-receptor agonist. The full residue-by-residue sequence is documented in the PubChem record referenced below rather than reproduced here.

rows: 44-residue GHRH(1-44) analogue with N-terminal hexenoyl modification

sections.reference_note: Identity data sourced from PubChem CID 16137828. Verify against the current PubChem record before publication, as database values are occasionally revised.

sections.heading: Ipamorelin: Scientific Identity
body: Ipamorelin (research synonym NNC-26-0161) is a synthetic pentapeptide studied as a selective growth hormone secretagogue, acting at the ghrelin receptor (GHSR-1a). Unlike tesamorelin, it is not a GHRH-pathway molecule; it is a separate class of compound entirely, distinguished in the literature partly by its selectivity for GH release without the broader hormonal effects reported for some older secretagogues.
sections.reference_note: Identity data sourced from PubChem CID 9831659. Verify against the current PubChem record before publication.

sections.heading: How Are Tesamorelin and Ipamorelin Studied?
body: Tesamorelin research centers on GHRH-receptor signaling: as a GHRH analogue, it is studied for its ability to bind GHRHR on pituitary somatotrophs and stimulate pulsatile growth hormone release, the same axis targeted by endogenous GHRH.
Ipamorelin research centers on the separate ghrelin/GHSR pathway: it is studied as a selective GHSR-1a agonist, stimulating GH release through a receptor and signaling cascade distinct from GHRHR.

Because GHRHR and GHSR-1a are both expressed on pituitary somatotrophs and both pathways converge on GH release, mechanistic literature on growth hormone secretagogues as a class discusses their pathways as biologically distinct at the receptor-biology level. That kind of pathway-level discussion is not the same as evidence that a specific combined formulation produces an added, additive, or synergistic effect in a study -- see Combination Evidence, below. This page does not provide dosage, timing, or co-administration guidance.

sections.heading: What Is Known About the Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin Combination?
body: No direct combination study was identified in the literature reviewed for this page. Published research on tesamorelin and published research on ipamorelin each exist as separate literatures, studying each peptide independently; no peer-reviewed study of tesamorelin and ipamorelin administered together, co-formulated, or evaluated as a combination product was located.

This matters because it is common, in market materials for combination peptides generally, to see evidence for each individual component presented as if it supports the combination. It does not. A finding about tesamorelin's effect on GH release says nothing, on its own, about what happens when tesamorelin is present alongside ipamorelin in the same formulation or research protocol. The reverse is equally true for ipamorelin.

Third-party laboratories and other vendors do issue Certificates of Analysis for 'Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin' or similar blend products, but a COA verifies chemical identity and purity of the material in a given lot -- it is analytical documentation, not biological evidence, and it does not represent a study of combined effect. Vera cue's own COA archive currently has no record for this or any product (see COA Status). No such document is being represented here as evidence of anything beyond what a COA can show.

tabs.label: Overview
body: Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin, as offered by Veracue, packages two independently sourced research peptides together: tesamorelin (TH9507), a 44-residue GHRH analogue, and ipamorelin, a five-residue ghrelin-receptor secretagogue. The two peptides differ in size, sequence, and the receptor pathway they are studied through.

Because they are different molecular entities, this page separates the documented identity and evidence for each peptide from any claim about the combination. Where the market commonly assumes a combined effect from the presence of two GH-pathway peptides in one product, this page makes clear that assumption is not, at present, supported by a direct study of the combination -- see Combination Evidence, above.

Composition specifics for this particular Veracue formulation -- ratio, per-vial content, concentration, and route -- are not yet published. Where a field is unconfirmed, this page states that plainly rather than inferring a value from the product name or from how other vendors describe similar 'tesa ipa' products.

sections.heading: Regulatory Context: Not the Same as an Approved Pharmaceutical
body: Tesamorelin, under the brand names Egrifta WR and Egrifta SV, is FDA-approved as a subcutaneous injectable for the reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy. The current prescribing information explicitly states it is not indicated for weight-loss management. That approval, and the clinical evidence behind it, applies to the specific approved pharmaceutical formulation, dose, and studied population -- it does not apply to the Veracue research material, which is a distinct, non-pharmaceutical RUO product with an unconfirmed formulation.

No FDA approval for ipamorelin as a pharmaceutical product was identified. Regulatory status for research compounds can change; researchers should verify current status independently rather than relying on supplier claims.

The Veracue Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin combination product is not FDA approved, is not evaluated by the FDA for safety or efficacy, and should not be assumed to share the formulation, concentration, route, dosing, or safety profile of any approved pharmaceutical product.

sections.heading: How to Read a Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin Certificate of Analysis
body: A combination product's COA needs to do more than a single-peptide COA: it should independently confirm the identity of both tesamorelin and ipamorelin in the same lot, not just one of the two. A COA for one component alone does not verify the presence, ratio, or purity of the other.

When this product's COA becomes available, it should state: identity confirmation for both peptides (by mass spectrometry, matched against each peptide's expected mass), lot/batch number, purity result and the analytical method used, any quantitative result for each component (not just an overall purity percentage), testing laboratory and test date, and the specific formulation the report describes.
quick_check_list: Lot number on the COA matches the vial label
Both tesamorelin and ipamorelin identity are independently confirmed, not just one component
Purity method is named for each component, not just a single blended percentage
Quantitative result (e.g., mg of each peptide) is reported, not only a purity percentage
Testing laboratory and date are shown
The report is matched to this specific formulation, not a generic single-peptide spec sheet

sections.heading: Research Use Only
body: Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin, as supplied by Veracue, is intended solely for laboratory and research use. It is not a drug, cosmetic, dietary supplement, or food. It is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease, and it must not be administered to humans or animals.

This page is not a weight-loss product page, a bodybuilding or performance product page, or a treatment guide. It contains no dosing, reconstitution-for-administration, injection, or protocol instructions for either component or for the combination, and none should be inferred from anything on this page.

faq.a: It is a Veracue research offering combining two separate peptides -- tesamorelin, a GHRH analogue, and ipamorelin, a ghrelin-receptor growth hormone secretagogue -- supplied together for laboratory research. It is not a single molecule and not a clinically validated combined product.

Tesamorelin (TH9507) is a synthetic 44-residue analogue of human growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), studied as a GHRH-receptor agonist. Under the brand names Egrifta WR and Egrifta SV, an approved pharmaceutical formulation is FDA-indicated for reducing excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy.

Ipamorelin is a synthetic pentapeptide studied as a selective growth hormone secretagogue that acts at the ghrelin receptor (GHSR-1a), a pathway distinct from GHRH signaling. No FDA-approved pharmaceutical product based on ipamorelin was identified.

faq.q: What is a tesa ipa blend?
faq.a: "Tesa ipa blend" is informal market shorthand for a tesamorelin-plus-ipamorelin research product. Veracue uses the descriptive name Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin because "blend" does not communicate a verified ratio, and this page does not treat any such term as evidence of a validated formulation.

faq.q: Is Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin the same as a tesamorelin pharmaceutical product like Egrifta?
faq.a: No. Egrifta WR and Egrifta SV are FDA-approved injectable pharmaceutical products containing tesamorelin alone, for a specific HIV-lipodystrophy indication. The Veracue Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin material is a two-peptide research product, is not FDA approved, and should not be assumed to share formulation, dosing, or safety data with the approved drug.

faq.q: How does tesamorelin work at the receptor level?
faq.a: Tesamorelin is studied as an agonist at the GHRH receptor (GHRHR) on pituitary somatotrophs, the same target as endogenous growth hormone-releasing hormone.

faq.q: How does ipamorelin work at the receptor level?
faq.a: Ipamorelin is studied as a selective agonist at the ghrelin / growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR-1a), a distinct receptor system from GHRHR.

faq.q: What is the difference between tesamorelin and ipamorelin?
faq.a: They are different molecules studied through different receptor pathways: tesamorelin is a 44-residue GHRH analogue acting on GHRHR, while ipamorelin is a 5-residue peptide acting on GHSR-1a. They differ in size, sequence, and mechanism -- they are not variants of the same compound.

faq.q: Is there direct research on the tesamorelin and ipamorelin combination?
faq.a: No direct combination study was identified in the literature reviewed for this page. Published research on each peptide exists independently; no study of the two administered or formulated together was located.

faq.q: Does research prove that tesamorelin and ipamorelin are synergistic?
faq.a: No. No direct combination study was identified, so no synergy claim is supported. Shared receptor biology at the pituitary level is a mechanistic observation, not evidence of a measured combined effect.

faq.q: What is the tesamorelin peptide sequence?
faq.a: Tesamorelin shares the 44-amino-acid sequence of human GHRH(1-44), with an added N-terminal modification (a trans-3-hexenoyl group on the tyrosine residue). The full residue-by-residue sequence is documented in PubChem (CID 16137828).

faq.q: What is the ipamorelin peptide sequence?
faq.a: Ipamorelin's sequence is Aib-His-D-2-Nal-D-Phe-Lys-NH2, a five-residue peptide with a C-terminal amide (PubChem CID 9831659).

faq.q: What should a Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin COA contain?
faq.a: It should independently confirm the identity of both peptides in the tested lot (not just one), report a quantitative result for each component, name the analytical method, and show the lot number, testing laboratory, and test date.

faq.q: What does purity mean for a two-peptide research product?
faq.a: Purity describes how much of the detected material, by a stated analytical method, is the intended compound rather than impurities or synthesis byproducts. For a combination product, purity should be reported for each peptide separately, since an overall figure can obscure a shortfall in either component.

faq.q: Is the Veracue Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin product FDA approved?
faq.a: No. It is not FDA approved and has not been evaluated by the FDA for safety or efficacy. It is supplied strictly for laboratory research use.

faq.q: What does Research Use Only mean for Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin?
faq.a: It means this material is intended strictly for laboratory and scientific research, not for human or veterinary administration, diagnosis, or treatment, and is offered and labelled on that basis.

acceptedAnswer.text: Purity describes how much of the detected material, by a stated analytical method, is the intended compound rather than impurities or synthesis byproducts. For a combination product, purity should be reported for each peptide separately, since an overall figure can obscure a shortfall in either component.

mainEntity.name: Is the Veracue Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin product FDA approved?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It is not FDA approved and has not been evaluated by the FDA for safety or efficacy. It is supplied strictly for laboratory research use.

acceptedAnswer.text: It means this material is intended strictly for laboratory and scientific research, not for human or veterinary administration, diagnosis, or treatment, and is offered and labelled on that basis.
